_purpose: CESC Electricity Tariff FY2025-26, FY2026-27 & FY2027-28 as printed in the booklet 'CESCOM Tariff Categories.pdf' (KERC Tariff Order 2025 dated 27.03.2025, Corrigendum 26.05.2025, Amendment 18.07.2025). Hand-transcribed from the 49 scanned pages (full text: '../../CESCOM Tariff Categories - transcription.md'). This file is the single source for every tariff category, rate and rule the app shows: the mart's mart_tariff_booklet_* tables (build_mart.py), the chatbot's tariff answers (app/tariff_booklet.py), the About glossary and the Tariffs page. Page numbers are the booklet's own.

source.title: Electricity Tariff for FY2025-26, FY2026-27 & FY2027-28
source.issuer: Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation Limited (CESC), Mysuru
source.order: KERC Tariff Order 2025 dated 27.03.2025; Corrigendum dated 26.05.2025; Amendment dated 18.07.2025
source.effective: Electricity consumed from the first meter reading date on or after 01.04.2025 (FY2025-26), 01.04.2026 (FY2026-27) and 01.04.2027 (FY2027-28).
source.area: All CESC consumers in Mysuru, Mandya, Chamarajanagara, Kodagu and Hassan districts.
source.caveat: CESC with other ESCOMs filed Review Petition No. 08/2025 before KERC seeking revision of tariff for LT-4(a), LT & HT industries and commercial categories; the booklet's rates are subject to the outcome.

parts.LT: Part I - Low Tension supply (400 V three-phase and 230 V single-phase). LT supply is given where the requisitioned load is less than 150 kW / 201 HP (page 5, para 9).
parts.HT: Part II - High Tension supply: bulk supply at 11 kV (including 2.3/4.6 kV) and above, at standard high or extra-high voltage, when the contract demand is 50 kW / 67 HP and above (page 30). Minimum HT contract demand 25 kVA (page 5).

categories.name: Domestic

categories.applies_to: Lighting / combined lighting, heating and motive power installations of residential houses, including the installations serviced under Bhagyajyothi / Kutirjyothi, and houses where a portion is used by the occupant for (a) handloom weaving, (b) silk rearing and reeling and artisans using motors up to 200 W, (c) consultancy in engineering, architecture, medicine, astrology, legal matters, income tax, chartered accountancy, (d) job typing, (e) tailoring, (f) post office, (g) gold smithy, (h) chawki rearing, (i) paying guests / home stay guests, (j) personal computers, (k) dhobis, (l) hand-operated printing press, (m) beauty parlours, (n) water supply installations and lifts independently serviced for bona fide use of residential complexes / residences, (o) farm houses and yard lighting limited to 120 W, (p) fodder choppers, arecanut cutting machines and milking machines with a connected load up to 1 HP. Also: (i) hospitals, dispensaries and health centres run by State / Central Government and local bodies; (ii) houses, schools and hostels meant for handicapped, aged, destitute and orphans; (iii) rehabilitation centres run by charitable institutions, AIDS and drug-addict rehabilitation centres; (iv) railway staff quarters with a single meter; (v) fire service station offices. notes: CDT = Commission Determined Tariff per kWh; it comprises a fixed-charge and a variable-charge component per unit.

If the Government of Karnataka does not release the subsidy in advance (Clause 6.1, KERC (Manner of Payment of Subsidy) Regulations 2008), the CDT shall be demanded and collected from these consumers.

The GoK shall release full subsidy to meet the revenue requirement on the approved quantum of IP-set sales (Section 65, Electricity Act 2003). On any shortfall, sales to IP sets of 10 HP and below are proportionately regulated or the ESCOMs collect the CDT from the IP consumers.
Electricity tax (9%) does not apply to agricultural IP sets up to and including 10 HP.
Energy only for pumping water to irrigate the consumer's own land (per the IP application / water-right certificate) and bona fide agriculture; otherwise billed under LT-3 / LT-5.
During disconnection only the fixed charges of the metered IP-set schedule are collected (LT-4(a), (b), (c), metered or not).
Billing at least once a quarter for all IP sets; capacitors per Clause 23 of the Conditions of Supply are mandatory (PF surcharge Rs 100/HP/year if missing).

rules.title: Interest on late payment
rules.text: Simple interest at 1% per month on the actual number of days of delay, subject to a minimum of Re 1 for LT and Rs 100 for HT installations. No interest is levied on arrears of Rs 10 or less. The bill must be paid within 15 days of presentation, failing which interest becomes payable (para 18).

rules.title: Order in which a payment is adjusted
rules.text: All payments are adjusted in this order: (a) interest on arrears of electricity tax, (b) arrears of electricity tax, (c) arrears of interest on electricity charges, (d) arrears of electricity charges, (e) the current month's dues.

rules.title: Reconnection charges
rules.text: Levied in case of disconnection and included in the monthly bill: (a) single-phase domestic installations under LT-1: Rs 20 per installation; (b) three-phase domestic installations under LT-1 and single-phase commercial & power installations: Rs 50; (c) all LT installations with three-phase supply other than LT-1: Rs 100; (d) all HT & EHT installations: Rs 500.

rules.title: Charges for a dishonoured cheque
rules.text: For each cheque not realised: up to Rs 10,000 - 5% of the amount (minimum Rs 100); Rs 10,001 to Rs 1,00,000 - 3% (minimum Rs 500); above Rs 1 lakh - 2% (minimum Rs 3,000).

rules.title: How bills can be paid
rules.text: Payments up to and including Rs 10,000 by cash, DD or digital payment; above Rs 10,000 by cheque, DD or digital payment. Bills can also be paid by ECS, debit / credit cards, RTGS / NEFT, net banking, the Karnataka One website and other RBI-compliant digital modes where the licensee provides them.

rules.title: Electricity tax
rules.text: Electricity tax at 9% ad valorem only on the consumption (energy) charges - excluding arrears, fixed charges / contract demand, D&R fee etc. - for all consumers except agricultural IP sets up to and including 10 HP (GoK notification DPAL 17 Shasana dated 19.07.2018; CESC circular dated 09.08.2018).

rules.title: HP / kW / kVA conversion
rules.text: For the tariffs: 1 HP = 0.746 kW; 1 HP = 0.878 kVA. Fractions of kW / HP are rounded to the nearest quarter kW / HP for billing, with a minimum of 1 kW / 1 HP for all LT categories including IP sets (street lighting: minimum a quarter kW).

rules.title: Rounding of the bill
rules.text: The bill amount is rounded off to the nearest rupee: 50 paise and above to the next rupee; less than 50 paise ignored.

rules.title: When supply is LT and when HT
rules.text: LT supply is given where the requisitioned load is less than 150 kW / 201 HP; the applicant may opt for HT supply for lesser loads. The minimum contract demand for HT supply is 25 kVA. HT tariffs apply to bulk supply at 11 kV and above when the contract demand is 50 kW / 67 HP and above. LT loads of 50 kW to 150 kW at 400 V need HT-class metering in a metering cubicle (para 31).

rules.title: HT billing demand
rules.text: The billing demand is the maximum demand recorded during the month or 90% of the contract demand, whichever is higher. Demand above the contract demand is charged at two times the normal rate per kVA per month (deterrent charges, Section 126(6) of the Electricity Act 2003); over-drawal is penalised at two times the normal rate. During a disconnection lasting the whole billing month the billing demand is 90% of the contract demand. Billing demand of 0.5 kVA and above is rounded up to the next kVA; below 0.5 kVA it is ignored.

rules.title: Power factor surcharge
rules.text: HT: the consumer must keep an average PF of at least 0.90; a surcharge of 3 paise per unit for every 0.01 below 0.90 lag. LT (LT-3, LT-4, LT-5, LT-6 with motive power): specified PF 0.85; surcharge of 2 paise per unit for every 0.01 below 0.85 lag, subject to a maximum of 30 paise per unit; 30 paise/unit if capacitors are below the Conditions-of-Supply requirement on inspection. PF = kWh / kVAh to 3 decimals then rounded to 2 (e.g. 0.8449 -> 0.84). Existing IP sets without adequate capacitors: PF surcharge Rs 100 per HP per year. Metered IP sets with capacitors get a 2 paise/unit rebate.

rules.title: Time-of-Day (ToD) tariff
rules.text: Compulsory for HT-2(a), HT-2(b) and HT-2(c) consumers with contract demand of 500 kVA and above; optional below 500 kVA, optional for HT-1, LT-5, and HT EV charging in KSRTC / NEKRTC / NWKRTC depots; not applicable to Railway Traction and BMRCL. Rates: July-November (monsoon) 0 in all hours; December-June: 06:00-09:00 +100 paise/unit, 09:00-18:00 0, 18:00-22:00 +100 paise/unit, 22:00-06:00 -100 paise/unit. ToD does not apply to energy billed under the Discounted Energy Rate Scheme beyond the base consumption.

rules.title: Rebate for supply at high voltage
rules.text: For supply above 13.2 kV: 33/66 kV - 2 paise per unit; 110 kV - 3 paise per unit; 220 kV - 5 paise per unit of energy consumed. Applies to normal energy (including ToD), not to wheeled energy or energy under SIS / DERS / other concessional schemes. Not applicable to BMRCL and Railway Traction.

rules.title: Incentive for prompt / advance payment
rules.text: An incentive of 0.25% of the bill, adjusted in the next month's bill: (i) for monthly bills above Rs 1,00,000 paid 10 days before the due date; (ii) for advance payments above Rs 10,000 towards monthly bills.

rules.title: Village panchayat rebate
rules.text: A rebate of 20 paise per unit for LT-3(a) commercial and LT-5 industrial consumers in village panchayat areas, excluding village panchayats within the jurisdiction of Urban Development Authorities.

rules.title: Rooftop solar (SRTPV) rebate
rules.text: LT domestic installations with sanctioned load up to 10 kW that have a solar rooftop PV system get a rebate of Rs 25/kW in fixed charges for the installed SRTPV capacity.

rules.title: Seasonal industries
rules.text: Needs an electronic tri-vector / smart meter. Working and off-season months are fixed by an order of the EE of the O&M division on the consumer's request and continue year to year (one month's notice to change). Off-season monthly consumption must not exceed 25% of the previous working season's average; off-season up to six months a year in at most two spells. HT: working season - demand charges on 90% of CD or recorded MD (higher); off season - on recorded MD or 50% of CD (higher). LT: off-season months pay energy charges plus 25% of the fixed charges. Fisheries ice / cold-storage plants within 5 km of the sea get 50% demand charges off season and a Re 1/unit rebate.

rules.title: Discounted Energy Rate Scheme (DERS)
rules.text: The Special Incentive Scheme was withdrawn from 01.04.2025. Under DERS, eligible HT-2a, HT-2b, HT-2c(i), HT-2c(ii), LT-3 (50 kW and above) and LT-5 (50 kW and above) consumers who opt in pay Rs 5 per unit for consumption above their base level. New opt-ins: base = average monthly consumption of FY2022-23 and FY2023-24 (or at least six months' data; new installations 67 units/kVA for HT, 57 units/kW for LT). Opted consumers get an additional 20% contract demand; consumption above base is outside FPPCA and ToD and is excluded when computing additional security deposit; open access must be relinquished. Extended for FY2025-26 at Rs 5/unit.

rules.title: Cross-subsidy surcharge (open access)
rules.text: Open-access consumers buying from generators / traders other than the ESCOMs pay a cross-subsidy surcharge in addition to wheeling charges (not for captive use). FY2025-26 paise/unit, e.g.: HT-1 112 (66 kV+) / 60 (HT); HT-2a 187; HT-2b 196 / 197; HT-2(c)(i) 185; HT-2(c)(ii) 191; HT-3 0; HT-4 179; HT-5 332; HT-6 204; HT-7 173; LT-1 83; LT-2 188; LT-3(a) 170; LT-3(b) 306; LT-4a 26; LT-4b 113; LT-4c 194; LT-5 148; LT-6 0; LT-7 321. The full three-year table is on booklet pages 45-47.

rules.title: Wheeling charges
rules.text: FY2025-26 wheeling (paise/unit, loss % in brackets): HT to HT 38 (0.48%), HT to LT or LT to HT 126 (7.44%), LT to LT 88 (6.96%); FY2026-27: 39 / 129 / 90; FY2027-28: 40 / 132 / 92. Additional surcharge is not levied until the Commission decides on BESCOM's petition. Green tariff: 50 paise per unit over the normal tariff for consumers opting for green power.

rules.title: Multiple connections and the single slab
rules.text: With the introduction of a single slab for energy charges, LT consumers may avail multiple connections to their premises; all meters of a building must be at one easily accessible place on the ground floor. The Commission also encourages self-reading of meters through digital modes (the licensee reads at least once in six months and reconciles).

rules.title: Who counts as a charitable institution
rules.text: Whether an institution is charitable is decided by the licensee on production of the Income Tax Form-10AC certificate.

rules.title: Temporary illumination in permanent premises
rules.text: Use of power for temporary illumination (marriages, exhibitions in hotels, sales promotions etc.) in premises that already have permanent supply is limited to the sanctioned load at the permanent tariff; temporary rates apply if the load exceeds the sanctioned load.

rules.title: Installations not covered by any schedule
rules.text: If an installation is not covered under any tariff schedule, the licensee may classify it under an appropriate schedule with intimation to and approval of KERC. The Conditions of Supply and the regulations under the Electricity Act 2003 prevail over the booklet in case of any discrepancy.

data_code_map._purpose: How each tariff code printed in the DCB sheets maps to the booklet's category (current structure, in force since the 2024-25 restructuring). Matched in order; 'match' is a case-insensitive regex on the printed code, 'desc' (optional) on the printed description.

rules.note: Up to 2023-24 the domestic lighting & heating slabs were LT-2(a); since 2024-25 they are LT-1.
Hoardings were printed as LT-7(b) up to 2023-24 and as LT-3(b) from 2023-24.
Government lift irrigation was HT-3(a)(i) up to 2023-24; HT-7 from 2024-25.
Irrigation & agricultural farms were HT-3b up to 2023-24; HT-6 from 2023-24.

data_lines._purpose: Lines the DCB sheets print that the booklet does not name separately, and the booklet category each belongs to.

lines.printed_as: LT-5(b) 'Heating & Motive Power - other than BMA' (by HP band)
lines.meaning: LT-5 Industrial. The booklet has only LT-5, with no sub-categories (no (a) / (b)); LT-5(b) is only how the DCB sheets print this division's industrial lines (LT-5(a) has no installations here). From 2024-25 LT-5 and LT-5(b) lines are billed at the same rate.

lines.printed_as: LT-2(a)(i)(FL) / LT-2(a)(ii)(FL) up to 2023-24; LT-1 '( Free Lighting)' from 2024-25
lines.meaning: LT-1 Domestic (single slab). A handful of installations (1-8) billed at the domestic rate and paid 85-95% by the Government subsidy (adjustment), even before Gruha Jyothi.

lines.printed_as: LT-3(i)(OL) / LT-3(ii)(OL) up to 2023-24; LT-3 a (i)(OL) / (ii)(OL) from 2024-25
lines.meaning: LT-3(a) Commercial, which covers 'all offices' (p.20). 13-15 installations billed at the LT-3 rate and paid 99-100% by adjustment every year.

lines.printed_as: LT-2(i)/(ii), LT-3 a (i)/(ii): 'in ULB's & CC' / 'in Village Pan.'
lines.meaning: The same category split by area: (i) urban local bodies and city corporations, (ii) village panchayats - the areas that get the booklet's 20 paise per unit village-panchayat rebate for LT-3(a) and LT-5.
